verdict.rationale: Bruno ships its own team-collaboration mechanism: collections are plain-text files shared through a built-in Git interface (init, diff, pull, commit, clone) inside the app, so teams can share and sync collections via a repository. However, Bruno explicitly says it is offline-only with no cloud sync, ever, so there is no automatically synced shared workspace, and syncing depends on users running Git pull/push. Missing for 10: real-time or automatic workspace sync, a hosted shared workspace, and independent hands-on corroboration of the team Git workflow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can share collections with my team in a synced shared workspace

citations.quote: Bruno's superpower is the ability to collaborate natively using version control systems like Git
Bruno's built-in Git interface — init, diff, pull, commit, and more without leaving the app.
Core Git UI features (init, view diffs, check for updates, pull, clone) are now available in the free version.
Bruno is offline-only. There are no plans to add cloud-sync to Bruno, ever.
saves API request collection files in simple, human-readable text files that are designed to be committed to a source control repo and easily shared
